title: Research notes — tides at Baisha
---

Research notes for chapters 4 and 5 (tides).

- Semi-diurnal tides: two highs and two lows a day. Spring tides fall near the new and full moon; the lowest of the year come with the autumn and winter new-moon springs.
- Based on the 1932 diary and the harbour tide tables, the entrance to the tide room under the south cliff is exposed only when the water drops below about minus 30 cm, i.e. on the lowest spring tides.
- The usable window is short: roughly forty minutes around dead low water. After that the flood returns at about a hand's width a minute, and the stair floods before the chamber does.
- Plot check: Lin Xiao's descent in chapter 5 is set on the first day of the tenth lunar month, low water 03:10, so she must be out by about 03:45.
- Typhoon low pressure plus offshore wind can push the water even lower than predicted (used in chapter 7).
